content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 2
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
30 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 1
**EMET (literal):** And-drew-near the-days-of David to-die, and-he-commanded ʾet-Solomon his-son, saying,

**LOGOS (formal):** When David's days drew near to die, he commanded Solomon his son, saying,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** As David's life neared its end, he gave Solomon his son these final instructions:

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 2
**EMET (literal):** "I am-going in-the-way-of all the-earth. And-be-strong, and-be a-man.

**LOGOS (formal):** "I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "I am about to die, as all people must. Be strong. Show that you are a man.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-keep the-charge-of YHWH your-God, to-walk in-his-ways, to-keep his-statutes and-his-commandments and-his-judgments and-his-testimonies, as-it-is-written in-the-Torah-of Moses, so-that you-may-prosper in-all that you-do and-in-all where you-turn,

**LOGOS (formal):** Keep the charge of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and keeping his statutes, his commandments, his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the Torah of Moses, that you may prosper in all that you do and wherever you turn,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Carry out the duties the LORD your God has given you. Walk in his ways. Keep his laws, his commands, his rules, and his decrees, as they are written in the Law of Moses — so that you will succeed in everything you do, wherever you go.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** so-that YHWH may-establish ʾet-his-word that he-spoke concerning-me, saying, 'If your-sons guard ʾet-their-way, to-walk before-me in-faithfulness, with-all their-heart and-with-all their-soul, saying, there-shall-not be-cut-off to-you a-man from-upon the-throne-of Israel.'

**LOGOS (formal):** that the LORD may establish his word that he spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your sons guard their way, to walk before me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not be cut off from you a man upon the throne of Israel.'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then the LORD will keep the promise he made to me: 'If your descendants are faithful to me, walking before me wholeheartedly, you will always have a man on the throne of Israel.'

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-do according-to-your-wisdom, and-do-not let-go-down his-gray-hair in-peace to-Sheol.

**LOGOS (formal):** Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Use your own judgment, but do not let him die a peaceful death.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** And-to-the-sons-of Barzillai the-Gileadite do ḥesed, and-let-them-be among-those-eating at-your-table, for so they-drew-near to-me when-I-fled from-before Absalom your-brother.

**LOGOS (formal):** But show loyal kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they drew near to me when I fled from Absalom your brother.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Show kindness to the sons of Barzillai of Gilead. Let them eat at your table, because they stood by me when I was fleeing from your brother Absalom.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-behold, with-you is Shimei son-of Gera the-Benjaminite from-Bahurim, and-he cursed-me a-grievous curse on-the-day-of my-going to-Mahanaim. And-he came-down to-meet-me at-the-Jordan, and-I-swore to-him by-YHWH, saying, 'I-will-not put-you-to-death by-the-sword.'

**LOGOS (formal):** And behold, there is with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And there is Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, who cursed me viciously the day I left for Mahanaim. When he came to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD that I would not kill him.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** And-now, do-not hold-him-guiltless, for a-wise man you are, and-you-will-know ʾet what you-should-do to-him, and-bring-down ʾet-his-gray-hair in-blood to-Sheol."

**LOGOS (formal):** Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You will know what you ought to do to him, and you shall bring his gray head down with blood to Sheol."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But you must not let him go unpunished. You are a wise man — you will know what to do. Make sure his gray head goes down to the grave in blood."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** And-David lay-down with his-fathers, and-was-buried in-the-City-of David.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then David slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then David died and was buried in the City of David.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** And-he-said, "A-word to-me to-you." And-she-said, "Speak."

**LOGOS (formal):** Then he said, "I have a word for you." She said, "Speak."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then he said, "I need to ask you something." "Go ahead," she said.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-he-said, "You know that to-me was the-kingdom, and-upon-me set all-Israel their-faces to-reign. But-the-kingdom turned-around and-became my-brother's, for from-YHWH it-was his.

**LOGOS (formal):** He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel had set their faces on me to reign. But the kingdom has turned and become my brother's, for it was his from the LORD.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine — all Israel expected me to be king. But things changed, and the kingdom went to my brother. It was the LORD's doing.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** And-now, one petition I am-asking from-you; do-not turn-away ʾet-my-face." And-she-said to-him, "Speak."

**LOGOS (formal):** Now I have one petition to make of you; do not refuse me." She said to him, "Speak."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Now I have just one request. Please don't turn me down." "What is it?" she asked.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-Bathsheba said, "Good; I will-speak for-you to the-king."

**LOGOS (formal):** Bathsheba said, "Very well; I will speak to the king on your behalf."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "Very well," Bathsheba said. "I'll speak to the king for you."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 20
**EMET (literal):** And-she-said, "One small petition I am-asking from-you; do-not turn-away ʾet-my-face." And-the-king said to-her, "Ask, my-mother, for I-will-not turn-away ʾet-your-face."

**LOGOS (formal):** She said, "I have one small petition to make of you; do not refuse me." The king said to her, "Ask, my mother, for I will not refuse you."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "I have one small request," she said. "Please don't turn me down." The king replied, "Ask away, Mother. I won't refuse you."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 23
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Solomon swore by-YHWH, saying, "Thus may-God do to-me and-thus may-he-add, for against his-own-life Adonijah has-spoken ʾet-this word.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, "May God do so to me and more also, for Adonijah has spoken this word against his own life.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then Solomon swore by the LORD: "May God strike me dead if Adonijah does not pay for this with his life!

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** And-now, as-YHWH lives, who established-me and-set-me upon the-throne-of David my-father, and-who made for-me a-house as he-spoke, for today Adonijah shall-be-put-to-death."

**LOGOS (formal):** Now therefore, as the LORD lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house as he promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** As surely as the LORD lives — the God who established me on my father David's throne and gave me a dynasty as he promised — Adonijah will die today."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Solomon sent by-the-hand-of Benaiah son-of Jehoiada, and-he-struck-him, and-he-died.

**LOGOS (formal):** So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him down, and he died.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** King Solomon gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who went and struck Adonijah down. He died.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 26
**EMET (literal):** And-to-Abiathar the-priest the-king said, "Go to-Anathoth, to your-fields, for a-man-of death you are. But-on-this day I-will-not put-you-to-death, because you-carried ʾet-the-ark-of the-Lord YHWH before David my-father, and-because you-were-afflicted in-all that my-father was-afflicted."

**LOGOS (formal):** To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you are a man worthy of death. But I will not put you to death at this time, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because you shared in all the affliction that my father endured."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** To Abiathar the priest, the king said, "Go home to Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I won't kill you now because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD for my father David and shared in all his hardships."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon drove-out ʾet-Abiathar from-being priest to-YHWH, to-fulfill ʾet-the-word-of YHWH that he-spoke concerning the-house-of Eli in-Shiloh.

**LOGOS (formal):** So Solomon expelled Abiathar from being priest to the LORD, thus fulfilling the word of the LORD that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** So Solomon removed Abiathar from the priesthood — fulfilling what the LORD had spoken long ago against the house of Eli at Shiloh.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 29
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was-told to-the-king Solomon that Joab had-fled to the-tent-of YHWH, and-behold, beside the-altar. And-Solomon sent ʾet-Benaiah son-of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike-him-down."

**LOGOS (formal):** It was told King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD and was beside the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike him down."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When Solomon was told that Joab had taken refuge at the altar, he sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada with orders: "Go and strike him down."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 30
**EMET (literal):** And-Benaiah came to the-tent-of YHWH and-said to-him, "Thus says the-king, 'Come-out.'" And-he-said, "No, for here I-will-die." And-Benaiah brought-back ʾet-word to-the-king, saying, "Thus spoke Joab, and-thus he-answered-me."

**LOGOS (formal):** So Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, "Thus says the king, 'Come out.'" But he said, "No, I will die here." Then Benaiah brought word back to the king, saying, "Thus said Joab, and thus he answered me."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Benaiah went to the tent of the LORD and said, "The king says, 'Come out.'" But Joab answered, "No. I will die here." Benaiah reported back to the king.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 33
**EMET (literal):** And-their-blood will-return on-the-head-of Joab and-on-the-head-of his-seed forever. And-to-David and-to-his-seed and-to-his-house and-to-his-throne there-will-be peace forever from-YHWH."

**LOGOS (formal):** Their blood shall return upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his offspring forever. But for David and his offspring and his house and his throne, there shall be peace from the LORD forever."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** May the guilt of their blood rest on Joab and his descendants forever. But may David and his descendants, his house and his throne, have the LORD's peace forever."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 36
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king sent and-called for-Shimei, and-said to-him, "Build for-yourself a-house in-Jerusalem and-dwell there, and-do-not go-out from-there anywhere.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then the king sent and summoned Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, and do not go out from there to any place.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then the king summoned Shimei and told him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not leave the city for any reason.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 37
**EMET (literal):** And-it-shall-be, on-the-day you-go-out and-cross ʾet-the-brook Kidron, know surely that dying you-shall-die. Your-blood will-be on-your-own-head."

**LOGOS (formal):** For on the day you go out and cross the brook Kidron, know for certain that you shall surely die. Your blood shall be on your own head."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The day you cross the Kidron Valley, you are a dead man. And it will be your own fault."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 38
**EMET (literal):** And-Shimei said to-the-king, "The-word is-good. As my-lord the-king has-spoken, so your-servant will-do." And-Shimei dwelt in-Jerusalem many days.

**LOGOS (formal):** Shimei said to the king, "What you say is good. As my lord the king has said, so will your servant do." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Shimei agreed: "That is fair. I will do as my lord the king says." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 39
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was at-the-end-of three years, and-two servants-of Shimei fled to Achish son-of Maacah, king-of Gath. And-they-told Shimei, saying, "Behold, your-servants are in-Gath."

**LOGOS (formal):** But at the end of three years, two of Shimei's servants fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And it was told Shimei, saying, "Behold, your servants are in Gath."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But three years later, two of Shimei's slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. When Shimei was told, "Your slaves are in Gath,"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 40
**EMET (literal):** And-Shimei arose and-saddled ʾet-his-donkey, and-went to-Gath, to Achish, to-seek ʾet-his-servants. And-Shimei went and-brought ʾet-his-servants from-Gath.

**LOGOS (formal):** So Shimei arose and saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to seek his servants. Shimei went and brought his servants from Gath.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** he saddled his donkey and went to Gath to get them back.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 42
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king sent and-called for-Shimei, and-said to-him, "Did-I-not make-you-swear by-YHWH, and-I-warned you, saying, 'On-the-day you-go-out and-walk anywhere, know surely that dying you-shall-die'? And-you-said to-me, 'The-word is-good; I-have-heard.'

**LOGOS (formal):** the king sent and summoned Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, saying, 'Know for certain that on the day you go out and walk about anywhere, you shall surely die'? And you said to me, 'What you say is good; I have heard.'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** the king summoned him. "Didn't I make you swear by the LORD?" he said. "Didn't I warn you clearly: 'The day you leave this city, you will die'? And you said, 'Fair enough. I agree.'

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 43
**EMET (literal):** And-why did-you-not keep ʾet-the-oath-of YHWH and-ʾet-the-commandment that I-commanded upon-you?"

**LOGOS (formal):** Why then have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the commandment that I commanded you?"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** So why didn't you keep the oath you swore before the LORD? Why did you disobey my command?"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 44
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king said to-Shimei, "You know ʾet-all the-evil that your-heart knows, that you-did to-David my-father. And-YHWH has-returned ʾet-your-evil upon your-own-head.

**LOGOS (formal):** The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your own heart all the evil that you did to David my father. Now the LORD will return your evil upon your own head.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The king continued, "You know in your heart every wicked thing you did to my father David. Now the LORD is bringing your wickedness down on your own head.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
